# Your task list stays accurate

This feature keeps your tasks accurate without anyone having to update them by hand. It notices new work that comes out of a conversation with the assistant, tracks what you have and have not looked at yet, and keeps your tasks in step with the tracker your team already uses, such as GitHub Issues or Jira. You spend less time copying information between tools and more time deciding what to do next.

## Contents

- [What it does for you](#what-it-does-for-you)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Good to know](#good-to-know)

## What it does for you

- Picks up new tasks automatically from conversations with the assistant, even ones that were only noted in a to-do list in a file.
- Marks work as unread when something changes, so you can see at a glance what is new and what has already been reviewed.
- Keeps your tasks in step with GitHub Issues or Jira: closing a task on one side closes it on the other, and the same goes for reopening.
- Groups related tasks under a bigger task, so finishing the bigger piece of work closes the smaller pieces tied to it too.
- Lets you mark something as read once you have looked at it, so it stops showing up as new.

## How it works

1. As you and the assistant work, new pieces of work are picked up and turned into tasks automatically.
2. When a task changes, such as its text or its status, it is marked as unread until someone reviews it.
3. You mark a task or a change as read once you have seen it, and it drops off the unread list.
4. If a task is linked to GitHub Issues or Jira, closing or reopening it in Imprimatur does the same on the tracker, and the other way around.
5. When a task is grouped under a bigger task, finishing the bigger one closes the smaller ones too.
6. The assistant also looks back over recent conversations and to-do lists to catch anything that should have become a task but did not.

## Good to know

- Only a short, fixed note is sent to GitHub or Jira when a task's status changes. The actual content of the task stays on your machine.
- Syncing with GitHub or Jira only works once your team has connected that tracker.
- Updates are checked regularly and also right after a change, so they usually show up within a few minutes rather than instantly.
- Catching tasks from past conversations only looks back over the last month.
